scenes.visual: Title card: The Casting Call.

scenes.tts: Every cell in a cluster can audition. What gives them that ability?
scenes.visual: A cluster of cells under a spotlight. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Every cell in a cluster can audition. What gives them that ability?

scenes.tts: The proneural genes were found in the fly. Two of them, akeety and scute, sit side by side on a chromosome.
scenes.caption: The proneural genes were found in the fly. Two of them, achaete and scute, sit side by side on a chromosome.
scenes.visual: A chromosome stretch labelled achaete-scute complex, with two neighbouring genes.
scenes.narration: The proneural genes were found in the fly. Two of them, achaete and scute, sit side by side on a chromosome.

scenes.tts: They are needed for the bristles on the fly's back.
scenes.visual: The fly notum with its rows of bristles.
scenes.narration: They are needed for the bristles on the fly's back.

scenes.tts: Predict. Remove these genes. What happens to the bristles? Then switch them on in extra places.
scenes.visual: Prompt card: Remove achaete-scute. Switch it on in extra places. Two blank notum outlines.
scenes.narration: Predict. Remove these genes. What happens to the bristles? Then switch them on in extra places.

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: Remove them, and bristles are missing. Switch them on in extra places, and extra bristles form.
scenes.visual: Reveal: one notum with bald patches, the other with extra bristles.
scenes.narration: Remove them, and bristles are missing. Switch them on in extra places, and extra bristles form.

scenes.tts: A related gene, atonal, was found in nineteen ninety-three. It does the same job for chordotonal organs.
scenes.caption: A related gene, atonal, was found in 1993. It does the same job for chordotonal organs.
scenes.visual: Name card: atonal, 1993. A chordotonal organ drawn inside the body wall.
scenes.narration: A related gene, atonal, was found in 1993. It does the same job for chordotonal organs.

scenes.tts: These are internal stretch receptors.
scenes.visual: The organ stretches as the body wall bends.
scenes.narration: These are internal stretch receptors.

scenes.tts: So different proneural genes start different kinds of sense organ.
scenes.visual: Two sense organs side by side: an external bristle and an internal chordotonal organ.
scenes.narration: So different proneural genes start different kinds of sense organ.

scenes.tts: Force akeety scute on, and only external sense organs form. Force atonal on, and mostly chordotonal organs form.
scenes.caption: Force achaete-scute on, and only external sense organs form. Force atonal on, and mostly chordotonal organs form.
scenes.visual: Two flies: extra bristles on one, extra chordotonal organs on the other.
scenes.narration: Force achaete-scute on, and only external sense organs form. Force atonal on, and mostly chordotonal organs form.

scenes.tts: A year later, atonal was shown to be needed for R eight. That is the founding photoreceptor of each eye unit.
scenes.caption: A year later, atonal was shown to be needed for R8. That is the founding photoreceptor of each eye unit.
scenes.visual: A compound eye; one unit enlarged, its first photoreceptor labelled R8.
scenes.narration: A year later, atonal was shown to be needed for R8. That is the founding photoreceptor of each eye unit.

scenes.tts: Without atonal, no R eight forms. The other seven photoreceptors, which R eight recruits, do not form either.
scenes.caption: Without atonal, no R8 forms. The other seven photoreceptors, which R8 recruits, do not form either.
scenes.visual: The eye unit empties: no R8, and the seven other photoreceptors missing.
scenes.narration: Without atonal, no R8 forms. The other seven photoreceptors, which R8 recruits, do not form either.

scenes.tts: All these genes encode the same kind of protein: a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor.
scenes.caption: All these genes encode the same kind of protein: a basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factor.
scenes.visual: Protein diagram labelled bHLH: a basic region, a helix, a loop, a helix.
scenes.narration: All these genes encode the same kind of protein: a basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factor.

scenes.tts: The helix-loop-helix part lets two proteins pair. The basic part grips DNA at a short sequence called an E-box.
scenes.visual: Two proteins pair like two hands, gripping a short DNA sequence labelled E-box.
scenes.narration: The helix-loop-helix part lets two proteins pair. The basic part grips DNA at a short sequence called an E-box.

scenes.tts: A proneural protein works with a partner. In the fly, that partner is Daughterless.
scenes.visual: The second hand is labelled Daughterless. In a corner: E proteins in vertebrates.
scenes.narration: A proneural protein works with a partner. In the fly, that partner is Daughterless.

scenes.tts: In vertebrates, the partners are called E proteins.
scenes.visual: Corner label grows: E proteins.
scenes.narration: In vertebrates, the partners are called E proteins.

scenes.tts: Vertebrates have relatives of both fly families. A S C L one is related to akeety scute.
scenes.caption: Vertebrates have relatives of both fly families. Ascl1 is related to achaete-scute.
scenes.visual: Family tree: achaete-scute to Ascl1 (Mash1); atonal to the Neurogenins and Atoh1.
scenes.narration: Vertebrates have relatives of both fly families. Ascl1 is related to achaete-scute.

scenes.tts: The Neurogenins, and a gene called Atoh one, are related to atonal.
scenes.caption: The Neurogenins, and a gene called Atoh1, are related to atonal.
scenes.visual: The atonal branch of the family tree lights up.
scenes.narration: The Neurogenins, and a gene called Atoh1, are related to atonal.

scenes.tts: So what decides where a cluster forms? In the embryo, clusters still form in the right places without Notch. Regulatory DNA around the akeety scute genes sets the map.
scenes.caption: So what decides where a cluster forms? In the embryo, clusters still form in the right places without Notch. Regulatory DNA around the achaete-scute genes sets the map.
scenes.visual: The embryo's ectoderm without Notch: clusters in their usual spots. Then the achaete-scute complex with switches drawn around the genes; each switch lights one cluster.
scenes.narration: So what decides where a cluster forms? In the embryo, clusters still form in the right places without Notch. Regulatory DNA around the achaete-scute genes sets the map.

scenes.tts: That map was worked out mostly on the notum and wing. There, Notch also helps shape the broader proneural stripes.
scenes.visual: The notum and wing, with cluster positions marked. A broad proneural stripe carries a small Notch label.
scenes.narration: That map was worked out mostly on the notum and wing. There, Notch also helps shape the broader proneural stripes.

scenes.tts: That answers the first puzzle. Proneural factors make a cluster able to become neural. Regulatory DNA places it.
scenes.visual: Puzzle card 1, Who may?, gets a check mark.
scenes.narration: That answers the first puzzle. Proneural factors make a cluster able to become neural. Regulatory DNA places it.

scenes.tts: Proneural factors say who may. Notch will say who does.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Proneural factors say who may. Notch will say who does.
scenes.narration: Proneural factors say who may. Notch will say who does.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
